agent.definition: A system in which a model decides, in a loop, which actions (tool calls) to take toward a goal, and when it is done.

tool.definition: A function, API or service an agent can call to read data or take an action. The model asks for the call; the runtime (or, for built-in tools, the provider's service) runs it.

workflow.definition: Control flow the designer defines in advance (sequences, branches, loops), possibly with model calls inside steps. A model may pick a predefined branch, but it never invents the path.

determinism spectrum.definition: The range of designs ordered by how much the system decides for itself: a chatbot acts only when the user asks, a workflow follows the designer's path, and an agent directs its own steps. More autonomy buys flexibility and costs predictability.

function calling.definition: A model capability: given function declarations, the model can return a structured request to call one of them with arguments, instead of text. The application or runtime executes the call and sends the result back.

function declaration.definition: The name, description and parameter schema that tell a model a tool exists and when to use it. In ADK it is generated from a function's name, docstring and type hints.

react.definition: Reason and act: a pattern in which a model alternates reasoning steps with actions such as tool calls, each result informing the next step (Yao et al., 2022).

max iterations.definition: A cap on how many times an agent loop may run, so a loop that is not converging stops. ADK counts it in model calls per run (max_llm_calls); a LoopAgent's max_iterations is a separate cap on cycles of a workflow loop.
